Alice (PM): Heads-up — I'm sketching an SLA-driven staggered rollout plan for the EU model switch. Need quick alignment on safe defaults (canary sizes, windows), automatic fallback policies, flag naming, and customer opt-out handling. Proposal below, please comment with hard constraints or blockers.

Raj (SRE): +1. Quick list of things we need from product to automate: target percentiles (p50/p95/p99), acceptable error rate delta, canary window, and circuit-break thresholds. Without numbers we can't set the autosurge/rollback triggers.

Maya (Eng): Draft numbers: p95 <= 200ms, error-rate delta <= 0.5pp, canary window min 30m with two consecutive windows of stable metrics to expand. For very latency-sensitive routes (edge TLs) tighten p95 to 150ms.

Tom (Sales): Heads-up from customers: enterprise tenants want opt-outs and a clear notification window. Standard ask: 14-day notice + per-tenant holdback flag. Can we support per-tenant feature flags for the rollout?

Alice (PM): Yes — plan includes per-tenant holdback. Also proposing three-phase rollout: 1) internal shadow (no user traffic) + synthetic perf; 2) small external canary (0.5% global or 1 region-localized); 3) gradual regional ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%). Requests: approvals for defaults and whether per-region semantics should be enforced or opt-in.

Raj (SRE): Operational constraints: autoscaling cushion must be provisioned for canary spikes. We need a default circuit-break: auto-fallback if p95 > 250ms for any 10-minute sliding window OR error-rate delta > 1% for 5 minutes. On fallback, route traffic to previous variant and notify #incidents + on-call.

Maya (Eng): Agree on auto-fallback. Also suggest a degraded fallback strategy: if full model variant fails, fallback to quantized/cheap model variant (same weights, lower resource) before routing to previous model. That gives faster recovery with less quality loss. Implementation note: model variants need compatibility tag to allow automated substitution.

Alice (PM): Good — include compatibility tags in model catalog. On the orchestration side, canary windows should be configurable per-rollout. Default naming for flags: `rollout/model/<model-name>/v<semver>/<region>` — does that work?

Raj (SRE): That naming is fine. One ask: separate flag for "holdback" vs "canary" so sales ops can toggle per-tenant holdbacks without flipping global canaries. Example commands we can support:

```
# enable canary globally for EU
yq e '.flags.rollout.modelX.eu = "canary:1%"' rollout.yaml | rui apply
# holdback tenant-123
redwood flags set tenant-123 rollout/modelX holdback=true
```

Maya (Eng): Also need telemetry contract: which metrics are required in the canary dashboard. Minimum: request_count, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, model_token_cost, and a simple semantic-regression signal (sampled eval prompts). The semantic check needs a small eval set run every 10 minutes (sampled, not full).

Tom (Sales): For customer-driven asks: some customers require a private deployment path (VPC) for the new model before we flip. We should document that as a gating condition in the rollout checklist for enterprise SKUs.

Alice (PM): I'll add to the launch checklist: 1) telemetry contract satisfied in staging, 2) sample semantic-eval pass (no quality regressions), 3) rollback runbook + automated rollback tested, 4) per-tenant holdback mechanism tested, 5) sales notified customers with opt-out flag link. Anything missing?

Raj (SRE): Add chaos tolerance test: simulated partial region outage with traffic re-routing to ensure fallback doesn't create oscillation. Also add a token-quota safety: if cost-per-token deviates > 30% we should trigger an alert and optionally throttle.

Maya (Eng): For A/B experiments during canary: recommend stat-sig window of at least 24h for quality metrics but allow quicker decisions for latency/cost SLOs. Map metrics to decision actions: latency/cost -> auto-fallback, quality sig -> manual rollback after review.

Alice (PM): Nice separation. Final question: can we safely automate region-level rollouts based on SLOs (no human in loop) for low-risk models, but keep human approval for enterprise-impacting models? Thoughts?

Raj (SRE): We can, but require an elevated threshold for fully-automated rollouts (longer observation windows and stricter SLOs). Otherwise keep a human gate.

Tom (Sales): From a contract perspective, we should default enterprise customers to manual approval unless they opt-in to auto updates in contract.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: rollout/modelX/v2 -> region=eu-west-1, initial=0.5% traffic, window=30m. Watch p95 and error_rate.

Alice (PM): Next steps: I'll update the rollout playbook with these defaults and a short runbook snippet. Raj/Maya — can you draft the exact thresholds and rollback plumbing by EOD so we can publish? Tom — I'll draft the customer notification template. Thanks all.
